defects: W7 wave 1 starts in week 26 with no steering review of the pilot record D9 (due week 25), so the first 10 pharmacies go live without a go/no-go on the pilot.
The week 27 check-in comes after waves 1 and 2 have started yet asks which pilot findings change waves 3 and 4, so pilot learnings never formally reach waves 1 and 2.
No step for vendor contract negotiation, hardware procurement or vendor mobilisation sits between the week 12 vendor selection gate and W5 configuration starting in week 13.
D11 final readout claims a go-live record for all 40 pharmacies but is due week 38 while W8 waves run to week 39, and no stabilisation period follows the last wave before the engagement closes.
W7 and W8 train pharmacy teams before each wave, yet no training materials or cutover/rollout plan appear as deliverables, and W2 and W4 are labelled 'after' W1 and W3 while overlapping them.

Workshop 1 takes the pilot go/no-go in week 21 while W5 setup runs to week 23 and reviews only D6 covering the first two process areas, so the pilot is approved before the configured system is complete.
No step for vendor contract negotiation, hardware procurement or vendor mobilisation sits between the week 12 vendor selection gate and W5 configuration starting in week 13.

D9 training materials are due week 29, after wave 1 training starts in week 28 and after the pilot pharmacy went live in week 24 without them, and are only reviewed at Workshop 2 after both waves have used them.
W1 runs to week 6 but has no final deliverable, with the consolidated requirements folded into W2's D2 due week 5, and the week 6 gate re-reviews the superseded interim D1.
D5 business case is due week 11, the same week as the D4 scoring it should build on, and its 'vendor comparison' duplicates D4.

why: Y puts a go/no-go on waves 1 and 2 straight after the pilot record and gives the client training materials, whereas X lets the first 10 pharmacies go live with no steering review of the pilot, the most consequential gap in either plan. X is cleaner on attendance tiering, pilot-readiness timing and its finance-owner note, but those strengths do not outweigh starting the scale rollout without reviewing the pilot.
